name: TimeTuna
tagline: A hosted time tracker for logging hours against projects and turning them into reports.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Time tracking is one of the most one-shottable categories in software: a timer, a projects table, a tags column, and a weekly rollup. An agent will give you that in a sitting, and for a solo freelancer the local version is often better because you can shape the report to match how you actually invoice. The gaps show up everywhere except the core loop: a phone app for when you start work away from the laptop, sync between machines, calendar and issue tracker imports so you are not typing project names by hand, and the small nags that stop you forgetting to hit stop. If anyone else needs to see your hours, or a client wants a branded PDF, you are now maintaining a product. Build it if you track your own time; pay if the timesheet is evidence for someone else.
coreLoopDIY: Runs a local web app where you start and stop a timer against a project and tag, edit entries by hand when you forget, and export a weekly or monthly total per project as CSV.
requirements: Node 20 and a machine you leave running or open daily
A browser tab you are willing to keep pinned
Willingness to fix your own forgotten timers
whatYouLose: Mobile app, so tracking off-laptop time means manual entry later
Sync across devices unless you host it somewhere and add auth
Calendar, issue tracker and repo integrations that pre-fill what you worked on
Idle detection, reminders and stop nags, which is the feature that actually keeps data honest
Client-ready invoices and shareable reports with someone else's logo on them
moatNotes: The defensible part of a time tracker is not the timer, it is the fifty small frictions removed between forgetting to start and having a defensible invoice.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay for time tracking because the data has to survive contact with someone else: a client disputing hours, an accountant, a manager, a court in the worst case. That means mobile capture, sync, backups, export formats other people accept, and enough polish that you actually log the time instead of reconstructing Thursday from memory. A local build nails the timer and fails the habit, because the habit is made of reminders and a phone in your pocket. If your hours are only for you, the local build is fine and free forever.
notes: The timer is trivial; remembering to press it is the entire product.
prompt:
Build a local-only personal time tracker called TunaLocal. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/time.db, created on first run
- Server actions for all writes, no separate API layer
- Runs with: npm install then npm run dev on port 3000

Data model:
- projects: id, name, client (nullable), hourly_rate (nullable), color, archived
- entries: id, project_id, description, tag (nullable), started_at, ended_at (nullable), created_at
- exactly one entry may have ended_at NULL at a time (the running timer); enforce it in the write path

Screens:
1. Today: big start/stop control, project picker, description field, optional tag. Live elapsed counter. List of today's entries with inline edit of start time, end time, project and description, plus delete.
2. Week: seven day columns, total hours per day, totals per project for the week, arrow keys or buttons to move between weeks. Show billable total when a project has an hourly rate.
3. Projects: create, rename, set rate, archive.
4. Export: date range picker, then download CSV (date, project, client, description, tag, start, end, hours) and a plain HTML print view for a range.

Rules and details:
- Store timestamps as ISO strings in UTC, render in the machine's local timezone.
- Allow manual entries with no timer, and allow entries that cross midnight (split them in reports, not in storage).
- Rounding is a display setting: exact, nearest 5 min, nearest 15 min. Default exact.
- If a timer has been running more than 10 hours, show a red banner asking if you forgot to stop it, with a one-click "end at" time fix.
- Keyboard: S starts or stops, / focuses the project picker.
- Seed script with three example projects and two weeks of fake entries so the week view is not empty.

Explicitly out of scope: auth, multi-user, mobile app, invoices with logos, Stripe, calendar or Jira or GitHub imports, idle detection, desktop notifications, any network call at all.

Write a README with setup, the backup instruction (copy data/time.db), and a short list of what was left out.
